profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, California, trading on the NASDAQ under the ticker NVDA. Its most recently reported annual revenue was $215,938,000,000, for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, as filed in a 10-K with the SEC under CIK 0001045810.

On the AI side, NVIDIA develops the Nemotron family of multimodal foundation models, which the company describes as designed for long-running, self-evolving agents capable of reasoning, multimodal vision, retrieval-augmented generation, speech processing, and safety tasks. Nemotron models are available under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which permits use, modification, distribution, and commercial deployment without requiring attribution to NVIDIA, and NVIDIA publishes the associated model weights, training datasets, and training techniques. Specific models in the family include Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, and routing is handled through NeMo Switchyard. The company notes that Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, is involved in shaping the Nemotron direction. Platform support includes NVIDIA RTX PRO and NVIDIA DGX Spark, and compatible open-source inference libraries include SGLang and vLLM.

NVIDIA also offers its NIM microservices product, a set of inference microservices for deploying foundation models in enterprise environments, available through build.nvidia.com and requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production use. Additional developer tooling referenced on the site includes NVIDIA Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, NeMo, and NVIDIA Blueprints. The held facts record no litigation or MCP server registry presence for the company at this time.
